items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: that was the beginning of the George Shearing Quintet — the original George Shearing Quintet — which was Denzel Best, Margie Hyams, Chuck Wayne, George Shearing and myself.

ctx.x: Yeah. You could see — you could probably see that it could be done a lot better.

Oh, yeah, and that really ticked me off because everything was backwards, you know. We didn’t get paid on time, and when you had to travel no arrangements were being made for it, and nothing. Everybody was on their own, you know, and I didn’t like it. So © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

when they left to go to California, I decided I was going to quit. So I left that group and this was about the time that I was just sort of like floating around. I got a call to come down to Birdland to work, finish out a week with Buddy Rich. Buddy Rich had a big band. So I went down to Birdland and worked the week with Buddy Rich and George Shearing was playing opposite Buddy Rich. items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We’ve got Denzil Best, Al McKibbon, Chuck Wayne, George Shearing, and myself. Traveling with us was George’s wife. Chuck Wayne’s wife was traveling with us.

ctx.x: How did you transition from playing to managing? How did that come about?

I realized that – after we made that first trip out and we were doing a lot of dates where we were working with a guarantee and a percentage – that – and I was acting as [the road manager] – Shearing’s wife was the road manager, considered the road manager, road person, but she had no experience at all and was at times very temperamental about things, really not suited to handle things like that. But in the meantime I was very close to her and advised her on everything. When she was doing the job, I was right…
